band_change_evidence_test.required: at least 2 independent sources with at least 1 at sourceTier >= 4
band_change_evidence_test.reason: FAIL. Four or more independent specialist sources converge on the same specific mechanisms, but every one sits at tier 1 to tier 2: gig-work review sites and worker forums. The SOMO report on unfair terms for AI data workers is tier 4 but is sector-wide and not specific to Labelbox. Labelbox cannot be verified at tier 4 in either direction, and the worker-condition findings should be treated as provisional pending higher-tier confirmation.

key_evidence: Labelbox scores lowest in this study, at 23.8, and it is the only one of the 15 where located adverse evidence, rather than missing disclosure, drives the result.

The evidence concerns Alignerr, Labelbox's AI-training crowdwork platform. Four independent specialist sources describe the same mechanisms: unpaid evaluation phases, pay gated on a reviewer accepting the work, accounts deleted without warning, and no appeal path that workers have found to work.

One review puts it concretely: if you spend five hours on tasks and the client closes the project before a reviewer reaches your queue, that work can go unpaid entirely. Workers report being owed $800 to $3,000 or more.

Every one of those sources sits at tier 1 or tier 2 — gig-work review sites and worker forums. The finding is corroborated but not verified at tier 4, and should be treated as provisional. SOMO's tier-4 research documents the same pattern across the sector, but not at Labelbox specifically.

Three subdimensions score the floor of 1: no appeal channel, a pay model that shifts risk onto the lowest-paid, and deactivation without explanation or alternative. Those are the only floor scores in this 600-subdimension study.

evidence.claim: Multiple independent sources report non-payment of $800 to $3,000 or more. Alignerr has documented patterns of deactivating workers before payment.

Evaluation phases are often unpaid, account deletions happen with no warning, qualified workers go months between projects, and voice work billed per finished hour collapses to about $9 per real hour worked.
If your account gets removed, it's permanent. There is no appeal path that workers have found to be effective.

If you spend five hours completing tasks and the client pauses or closes the project before a reviewer gets to your queue, that work can go unpaid entirely. It is not a scam, but it is a structural risk baked into the pay model.
Big Tech sets unfair terms and conditions for AI data workers globally. This report addresses the sector rather than Labelbox specifically.
evidence.source: SOMO, 'Big Tech sets unfair terms and conditions for AI data workers globally'

evidence.claim: Google's Cloud business has a partnership with Labelbox, the company behind the crowdwork platform Alignerr, to provide human evaluation services for AI.
evidence.source: Built In on AI training gig work

notes: FLAG FOR REVIEW — NOT A DOWNGRADE. No score change is proposed for application. The published 48.4 is a never-assessed uniform-seed placeholder shared byte-for-byte with seven other ai-labs entities at consecutive alphabetical ranks; the rank is an artefact of the tie. 3 subdimensions rest on positively documented failure; the remainder of the gap is missing disclosure. Applying a one-off baseline reset on evidence-absence alone would convert a calibration problem into a conduct finding, which the anti-false-positive screen forbids. Referred for coordinator-level calibration of the ai-labs 60.9 and 48.4 uniform-seed clusters. rotation-state composite/band/rank left at the PUBLISHED values.
